_nota: Inglés del Paso 8 · El abordaje quirúrgico. Calco parcial. Los abordajes epónimos conservan su nombre propio (Kocher, Henry, Thompson, Kocher-Langenbeck…), que es como se citan en cualquier idioma.
subtitulo: The approach serves the biomechanical principle, not the other way round
preguntaClave: Does this approach give access to what I have to do, and is it consistent with the biology I decided to preserve?
sintesis: The approach is chosen for what you want to achieve and it must match the principle from Step 5: extensile to reconstruct and compress, minimally invasive to bridge, combined when there are two zones. The soft tissues determine the result as much as the fixation does: full-thickness flaps, periosteum respected, an internervous plane and a tension-free closure. And the structure at risk of each route is part of the plan, not an intraoperative surprise.

esencial.texto: The approach is chosen for what you want to achieve, not out of habit. It has to give enough access to the fracture and to the fixation points while respecting the blood supply and the neurovascular planes as far as possible. The AO's governing principle is clear: handling of the soft tissues determines the result as much as the fixation does.

Full-thickness flaps: dissect down to the deep plane and handle the tissue as a block, without raising layers, to preserve skin perfusion. Respect the bone's blood supply: avoid circumferential periosteal stripping, because every millimetre of devitalised periosteum is biology lost. Work through internervous planes: entering between territories of different nerves avoids denervating muscles. And do not close under tension: dehiscence and edge necrosis open the door to infection.

esencial.titulo: Types of approach and consistency with the principle
filas: Direct anatomical reduction: articular fractures and lines to be compressed.
It accepts more exposure in exchange for precision.
Small windows, submuscular tunnel, preserves the haematoma.
It reaches more than one column or facet.

esencial.texto: If the plan is to bridge — relative stability, functional reduction — a wide approach that strips the fracture betrays the strategy. If the plan is to rebuild an articular surface, an inadequate window makes anatomical reduction impossible. The approach serves the biomechanical principle, not the other way round.

esencial.titulo: The structure at risk is known beforehand, not discovered inside
esencial.texto: Every classic approach exploits an interval between muscles of different innervation and keeps a safe zone with respect to the vital structures. The radial nerve in the posterior humerus and the proximal forearm, the axillary nerve 5 cm from the acromion, the ulnar nerve in every elbow approach, the supraclavicular nerves at the clavicle, the suprascapular nerve in the posterior scapula, the sciatic nerve in the posterior hip and acetabulum. Knowing which structure is at risk is part of the plan, not an intraoperative surprise.

esencial.texto: Single or double incision: in two-bone fractures — forearm, pilon with fibula — separate incisions with the skin bridge respected prevent necrosis and, in the forearm, synostosis. And wait for the soft-tissue window: in critical regions, postpone the incision until the swelling settles and the wrinkle sign appears. The timing decision taken in Step 1 becomes real here, with the scalpel in hand.

Positioning and approach prepare the execution. The position is chosen so that the approach, the reduction and the imaging are possible; the approach is chosen to serve the biomechanical principle with the least damage to the soft tissues. Both must be consistent with everything decided before: the best implant is worthless through an inconsistent route or in a position that makes reduction impossible.

alertas.titulo: Handling of the soft tissues determines the result as much as the fixation
alertas.texto: It is the AO's governing principle in this step. Full-thickness flaps, periosteum respected, internervous plane and tension-free closure.

alertas.titulo: You are going to bridge and you are opening the fracture
alertas.texto: In Step 5 you chose splinting, which heals by callus and lives off intact biology. An extensile approach over that zone destroys the fracture haematoma and the periosteal blood supply the callus needs. The approach betrays the strategy: the consistent route is MIPO.

alertas.titulo: Anatomical articular reconstruction through a minimally invasive route
alertas.texto: An articular surface is rarely rebuilt blind. If you go by MIPO, make sure you have arthroscopy, intraoperative CT or a dedicated articular window; otherwise the window is inadequate and the step-off stays inside.

alertas.titulo: The percutaneous approach does not reduce: it only fixes
alertas.texto: It assumes the reduction has already been achieved closed. If it has not, you are going to fix a badly reduced fracture with the advantage of not seeing it.

alertas.titulo: The soft-tissue window is not open
alertas.texto: With swelling, blisters or tight skin, cutting now leads to edge necrosis, dehiscence and deep infection. Spanning external fixator and wait for the wrinkle sign. This is the Step 1 decision becoming real.

alertas.titulo: Two bones and a single incision
alertas.texto: In the forearm and in the pilon with fibula, a single incision compromises the skin bridge. In the forearm it also adds the risk of radioulnar synostosis. Use separate incisions.

alertas.titulo: Respect the skin bridge
alertas.texto: The narrower it is, the greater the risk of necrosis of the flap between the incisions. Plan both incisions before the first one, not after.

alertas.titulo: You have not planned a tension-free closure
alertas.texto: Dehiscence and edge necrosis are the door to deep infection, and in subcutaneous regions — tibia, calcaneus, ankle — they decide the result. If in the end it will not close without tension, do not close it: delayed closure or coverage.

alertas.titulo: Circumferential periosteal stripping is biology lost
alertas.texto: Opening widely and then stripping the periosteum all the way round leaves the fragment with no source of blood supply at all. It is the mechanism by which a technically correct fixation ends in non-union.

alertas.titulo: The L-shaped calcaneal flap does not forgive
alertas.texto: It is raised full thickness, without touching the subcutaneous plane, and it is not retracted with retractors: it is held with bent Kirschner wires. Necrosis of the apex is the complication that decides the result of this operation.

alertas.titulo: Identify the radial nerve before putting in the plate
alertas.texto: In the posterior humeral approach the nerve crosses the field in the spiral groove. Finding it first and protecting it is quicker than looking for it once a plate is already on top.

alertas.titulo: Sciatic nerve offloaded throughout the operation
alertas.texto: In the Kocher-Langenbeck, knee flexed and hip extended from beginning to end. Sciatic injury in this approach is almost always from sustained retractor traction, not from division.

alertas.titulo: The nail entry point decides the deformity
alertas.texto: An eccentric portal deforms the proximal fragment the moment the nail goes in, and that deformity cannot be corrected afterwards. Check it in two planes before reaming.

alertas.titulo: Work through the internervous plane
alertas.texto: It is the whole reason the classic approaches exist: entering between territories of different nerves lets you separate muscles without denervating them. If you leave the interval, the muscle you cross loses its nerve supply.

alertas.titulo: The lateral plate does not control the medial fragment
alertas.texto: A Schatzker IV, or a medial or posteromedial column involved, needs its own buttress through its own approach. Holding them with long screws from a lateral plate is the mechanism by which these fractures collapse into varus within weeks.

alertas.titulo: In the acetabulum, the approach is the operation
alertas.texto: The Letournel pattern does not describe: it prescribes. Choosing the wrong route is not corrected by extending the incision, and the combined or extensile approach has a soft-tissue cost that has to be accepted before starting.

alertas.titulo: You marked the anterolateral quadrant and you are not approaching it
alertas.texto: The anterolateral quadrant is reached through the lateral approach. Without that window, the split-depression is reduced blind. What fits is the lateral approach to the proximal tibia, alone or combined with the one you already chose.

alertas.titulo: You marked the anteromedial quadrant and you are not approaching it
alertas.texto: The anteromedial plateau is not held by a lateral plate: it works in shear and gives way into varus. It needs its own medial window and a buttress. What fits is the medial approach to the proximal tibia, alone or combined with the one you already chose.

alertas.titulo: You marked the posterolateral quadrant and you are not approaching it
alertas.texto: The posterolateral quadrant lies behind the fibula: it can be neither seen nor instrumented from the front. Either it is approached from behind, or that depression is left unreduced. What fits is the posterolateral approach to the proximal tibia, alone or combined with the one you already chose.

alertas.titulo: You marked the posteromedial quadrant and you are not approaching it
alertas.texto: The posteromedial fragment subluxes in flexion and no anterior plate controls it. It is the one most often forgotten and the one that most often fails. What fits is the posteromedial approach to the proximal tibia, alone or combined with the one you already chose.

alertas.titulo: In the plateau, each quadrant asks for its own window
alertas.texto: Schatzker as modified by Kfuri divides the plateau into four quadrants — anterolateral, anteromedial, posterolateral and posteromedial — precisely because each one is reached from a different place. That is the value of the classification: it does not describe, it plans the approach. Two broken quadrants usually mean two windows, with the skin bridge thought out from the start.

reglasCoherencia.titulo: Consistency — the named approach is missing
reglasCoherencia.mensaje: You have defined the kind of approach but not the specific route. The internervous plane and the structure at risk depend on that choice, and they are part of the plan, not an intraoperative surprise.
Minimally invasive fixation replaces direct vision with imaging. Check that in Step 7 you settled C-arm access to every projection you are going to need.

reglasCoherencia.titulo: Consistency — extensile approach with a doubtful window
reglasCoherencia.mensaje: An extensile approach over soft tissues that are not ready. It is the combination that produces edge necrosis and deep infection. Spanning external fixator and wait for the wrinkle sign.

evidencia.afirmacion: In distal tibial and femoral fractures, minimally invasive fixation achieves healing comparable to open reduction with fewer soft-tissue complications and less infection.
Every classic approach exploits an internervous interval and defines a safe zone with respect to the vital structures.

autoevaluacion.pregunta: Why can a wide approach betray the plan?
opciones: Because it lengthens the operating time
Because if the principle is to bridge — relative stability, which thrives on intact biology — stripping the fracture destroys the blood supply the callus needs
Because it makes the plate impossible to apply
autoevaluacion.explicacion: The approach serves the biomechanical principle, not the other way round. If you are going to bridge, enter through small windows.

autoevaluacion.pregunta: Name the structure at risk in the posterior humeral approach.
opciones: Radial nerve in the spiral groove
autoevaluacion.explicacion: It has to be identified BEFORE the plate is applied, not once hardware is already on top.

autoevaluacion.pregunta: Which manoeuvre moves the posterior interosseous nerve away from the field in the lateral elbow approach?
autoevaluacion.explicacion: Pronation moves the nerve, which runs within the supinator, laterally and away from the dissection.

autoevaluacion.pregunta: In a both-bone forearm fracture, why two separate incisions?
opciones: Because the hardware will not fit through one
To respect the skin bridge and reduce the risk of necrosis and of radioulnar synostosis
Because the internervous plane demands it
autoevaluacion.explicacion: The same criterion applies to the pilon with fibula: separate incisions and the skin bridge respected.

autoevaluacion.pregunta: What does the wrinkle sign mean?
opciones: That the swelling has settled and the skin creases again: the soft-tissue window is open
autoevaluacion.explicacion: It is the clinical criterion for moving from a spanning fixator to definitive fixation in critical regions.

opciones: Because handling the tissue as a block, without raising layers, preserves skin perfusion
Because it speeds up the dissection
autoevaluacion.explicacion: Every plane you separate is a blood supply lost. It is what decides the viability of the wound edge.

autoevaluacion.pregunta: In the Kocher-Langenbeck, how is the sciatic nerve protected?
opciones: With the knee flexed and the hip extended throughout the operation
With the hip flexed and the knee extended
autoevaluacion.explicacion: That position offloads it. Injury in this approach is almost always from sustained retractor traction, not from division.
